## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), also cited as *Guttilavimāna*, is a canonical verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [von Hinüber 1996]. In this text, multiple celestial beings discuss the meritorious actions they performed during their past human lives that led to their rebirth in happy celestial realms. As recorded in the commentary to the *Guttilajātaka* (Ja 243), the Bodhisatta visits the celestial realm and questions thirty-seven goddesses (*devadhītā*) who appear in the *Guttilavimānavatthu*, each explaining in verse the specific karmic deeds—such as offering almsfood or water, maintaining virtue, and serving without anger—that caused their rebirth as companions to the king of gods [Fausböll 1879].

Cross-textual connections link this narrative directly with the *Guttilajātaka* (Ja 243).

- [von Hinüber 1996] Oskar von Hinüber, A Handbook of Pāli Literature (1996) — Attests the alternative title form Guttilavimāna.
